findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment:
Observed the following instances of improper storage:
(i) 1ST REPEAT: Soup/Salad bowls were stored on open shelves near the prep line upright instead of inverted, and are open to falling debris through the upper shelves. PIC was notified and plans to place mats on the upper shelves to protect the dishes and prevent falling debris, as the shape of the bowls does not allow for inversion.
(ii) Clean bowls and other dishes were stored in the dish room in the open and upright position instead of protected or inverted. Of particular concern were large metal bowls that were air-drying where the water inside was not able to drain because they were not inverted. CORRECTED: the bowls were inverted during the inspection, and PIC was notified that all clean articles need to be protected by inversion or a cover.
Ensure all equipment, utensils, and single-service or single-use articles are kept protected through cover or inversion.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed several items that were being stored past their date-marked discard date. PIC voluntarily disposed of the items. It is important that items not only are properly date-marked with the day of prep being day 1 and day 7 being the date where the item must be used or discarded, but that out-of-date items are then discarded per the written date-mark.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following instances of improper storage:
1) bowls were stored on open shelves upright instead of inverted and were open to falling debris through the shelves;
2) utensils were stored upright instead of inverted in the drying racks.
The PIC was notified of all instances.
1) The shape of the bowls is not conducive to inversion, so the PIC plans to place mats on the above shelves to protect the dishes and prevent falling debris.
2) The utensils were removed and washed and replaced in an inverted position.
It is important that all equipment, utensils, and single-service or single-use articles are kept protected through cover or inversion.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed a build-up of debris in the following locations:
1) (1ST REPEAT) The debris on the floor of the outside shed that stores single-use articles.
2) The debris surrounding the microwave in the front kitchen area.
3) The splashes and debris in the bottom of both milk coolers.
4) The debris surrounding the bread slicer.
The PIC was notified and planned to add it to the cleaning schedule.
It is important that food-contact and non-food contact surfaces are kept free of accumulated dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of black mold and deterioration of caulking near the dish machine and triple sink. PIC was notified and made plans for cleaning and re-caulking. It is important that all physical facilities be maintained and in good repair, and that equipment that cannot be moved is kept sealed to prevent the building of moisture and debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces: 

(1) The caulking on the back of house coffee table is disconnected on the right side causing a gap between the wall and table. The table must be properly caulked because it cannot be removed from the wall for cleaning. The caulking on the right side must be replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface.

(2) There are several small holes in the wall within the dish washing room. The holes are from shelving that was removed. The holes must be filled (ex.caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface.

Ensure that the above referenced are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned: 

(1) The accumulation of soil debris behind the soda nozzles on the drive through and customer drink dispensers. 

(2) The dust on the shelves holding clean dishes and equipment above the non-functioning prep coolers in the dish washing room. 

(3) The debris on the floor of the outside shed that stores single-use articles. 

Ensure that the above referenced non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the floors of the main walk-in cooler have an accumulation of debris (including, but not limited to, dust, trash, and food). The floors must be cleaned underneath the shelving against the wall. The inspector suggests pulling out the shelving to clean the hard-to-reach areas. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.
